'''Yuri Timofeevich Struchkov''' ({{langx|ru|Юрий Тимофеевич Стручков}}) <ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | url=https://www.iucr.org/people/crystallographers/yuri-timofeevich-struchkov-1926-1995 | title=Yuri Timofeevich Struchkov (1926-1995) | journal=Acta Crystallogr. (1996). A52, 329-330  |last=Kalman |first=Alajos}}</ref>(28 July 1926, [[Moscow]] — 16 August 1995, [[Charleston, South Carolina]]) was a Russian and Soviet chemist. He was a prominent scientist in the field [[X-ray crystallography]], a Corresponding Member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (1990) and the vice-president of the [[International Union of Crystallography]] (1993-1995).<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://journals.iucr.org/a/issues/1995/04/00/a28031/a28031.pdf | title=International Union of Crystallography, Sixteenth General Assembly and International Congress of Crystallography, Beijing, China, 21-29 August 1993 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | url=https://www.iucr.org/news/newsletter/etc/articles?issue=151351&result_138339_result_page=25 | title= Yuri T. Struchkov: commemorating his 95th birthday. | journal = IUCr Newsletter |date=2021 |issue=2 |page=25}}</ref> Struchkov was the founder and the first Director of the X-Ray Structural Laboratory of [[Nesmeyanov Institute of Organoelement Compounds]] and X-Ray Structural Centre of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (RAS). He made important contributions to the fields of chemistry and crystallography of organic, organoelement and coordination compounds. As an author and co-author of more than 1000 papers, published between 1980 and 1990, he became the most widely published scientist of the decade.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Abrahams |first=Marc |date=2008-03-11 |title=Man at work |url=http://www.theguardian.com/education/2008/mar/11/highereducation.research |access-date=2022-08-02 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref> In 2021, the [[International Union of Crystallography]] (IUCr) honored his contributions to the field of small molecule structural crystallography, establishing the Struchkov Prize,<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.iucr.org/iucr/struchkov-prize#:~:text=The%20Struchkov%20Prize%20will%20be,crystal%20chemistry%2C%20or%20material%20science. | title=Struchkov Prize. History and background }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | url=https://www.iucr.org/news/newsletter/etc/articles?issue=150867&result_138339_result_page=27 | title=Struchkov Prize moves to the IUCr | journal = IUCr Newsletter |date=2021 |issue=1 |page=27}}</ref> which is awarded to the young crystallographers at the regular triennial IUCr International Congress of Crystallography.

== Scientific career ==

* In 1948 Struchkov graduated  from the  [[MSU Faculty of Chemistry]].
* In 1948—1953 he was a working on his Ph.D. thesis under the supervision of professor [[Китайгородский, Александр Исаакович|A.I.Kitaigorodski]].
* In 1950 he joined the staff of the [[Институт органической химии АН СССР|Zelinsky Institute of Organic Chemistry]] (IOCh).
* In 1953 he defended the PhD thesis ''X-Ray structural study of two addition products of metal salts to unsaturated compounds''.
* In 1954—1995 he worked in the  [[Nesmeyanov Institute of Organoelement Compounds]] (INEOS):
** in the laboratory headed by A.I.Kitaigorodski (1954–1973)
** in the diffraction studies group (1973–1977)
** in the new Laboratory of the X-Ray Structure Analysis (LXRSA) which was founded and headed by him (1977–1995).
* In 1989 Struchkov became the Director of the X-Ray Structural Centre of RAS, which was based on the INEOS LXRSA.
* In 1990 he was elected Corresponding Member of RAS and a member of the executive committee of the [[International Union of Crystallography]] (IUCr).
* At the XVI  General Assembly of IUCr in 1993 he became the vice-president of the IUCr (1993–1995).
